summary: Carney and EU leaders open a Montréal summit aimed at an 'ever closer association', and Ottawa says it will invest up to $1.6 billion in Toronto AI company Cohere.
body: Prime Minister Mark Carney opened a two-day Canada-EU summit in Montréal on Thursday with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa [^2][^3]. The two sides are working toward an "Alliance for the Future" covering trade, critical minerals, energy, AI, research and security, including Canadian access to EU programs such as Horizon research funding and Erasmus exchanges [^1][^3]. Carney said Canada is working to become an "associate member" of the EU, while ruling out full membership and saying any deeper partnership would face a vote in Parliament; von der Leyen called it "an association without accession" [^1][^3]. Hours before the trip, Germany pushed to take "associate membership" out of the joint declaration, which now speaks of "ever closer association" [^1].

The concrete pieces so far: Costa said a digital trade agreement would be approved today, and von der Leyen said a deal would give Canadian companies and researchers access to the EU's 12 supercomputers [^2][^3]. Carney also announced that Ottawa will invest up to $1.6 billion in Cohere, a Toronto AI company, which will in turn invest at least $1.7 billion in new computing infrastructure in Canada; the government would not say how large a stake it gets [^2][^3]. The EU also wants Canada to help close a €70-billion gap in Ukraine's 2027 budget [^1].

Why it matters at home: the US bought 71.7% of Canada's goods exports last year, so closer ties with Europe are a way to spread that risk [^3]. A TD Bank report found demand for nearly $60 billion more in Canadian exports to the EU [^2]. My read: the deals are real but modest so far, and what "associate" status means in practice depends on what is signed today.
differences: Trump has suggested the arrangement could be a "hostile act" and threatened tariffs on Europe, though on Thursday he said Canada had been treating the US "extremely nicely" lately [^2][^3]. Carney says the US will "see the benefit" [^2]. In Europe, France and Germany are uneasy with the "associate member" label [^1][^3].

reads.title: EU and Canada to seal new alliance in Montréal under Trump's shadow
reads.summary: What the EU and Canada hope to sign in Montréal, from minerals and AI to Ukraine funding, and why Germany objected to the 'associate membership' wording.
